about: Committed MusicXML files that may fail `python tests/bench/run.py sg-roundtrip` (docs/GOALS/G01 §16.2, A34): at most three, each with the reason and a minimal fixture that reproduces the same difference. sg-roundtrip checks that each fixture still fails.

files.detail: Bar 16 closes a second-ending bracket (<ending number="2" type="stop"/>) that never opens. The app records the stop on the bar (endingNos [2], endingEnd 'stop'), so the G0 projection of the bar changes (L1 STRUCTURAL_CHANGE, and L1+ loses the ending row). A ScoreGraph Ending has both ends (G01 §5.4); the import reports the orphan stop as dropped ('ending (stop without start)'). The play order is the same: a stop alone opens nothing.

Bar 76 stops a wedge that never started and bar 77 starts a diminuendo that never stops. A ScoreGraph Wedge has both ends (G01 §5.10); the import reports both marks as dropped ('wedge (stop without start)', 'wedge (unclosed)'). L1 passes because the G0 projection (semantic/3) carries no dynamics or wedges — not because the marks do not matter: the app reads <wedge> and builds its playback intensity from it, and a diminuendo that never stops is ramped to the end of the piece. Only the notation inventory sees the loss (L1+). G1 production never imports MusicXML, so nothing sounds different today; when import moves onto the graph this becomes audible and the entry has to be looked at again (G01 §26, F3).
